question: A single normal Antistreptolysin O (ASO) titre is sufficient to rule out recent Group A Streptococcal pharyngitis in a patient with suspected rheumatic fever.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect — the statement is actually false. ASO peaks 3–5 weeks post-pharyngitis and may already be falling when RF presents. A single normal titre cannot exclude recent GABHS. Always order both ASO and anti-DNase B together to avoid missing a true positive.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is false. ASO titres peak 3–5 weeks after pharyngitis and may already be declining by the time RF manifests (2–4 weeks post-infection). Always request both ASO and anti-DNase B to maximise sensitivity; a single normal ASO does NOT rule out recent GABHS infection.
